title: Steering with a system prompt and examples

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model.

tasks.title: Ask for a bare label
tasks.description:
Ravi wants every inbox message tagged with one of five labels: `watering`, `light`, `pests`, `order`, `other`.

1. Write `LABEL_PROMPT`: a system prompt that says who the model is, names all five labels, and tells it to reply with **only** the label.
2. Implement `labelMessage(text: string, client?: OpenAI): Promise<Label>`. Send `[system: LABEL_PROMPT, user: text]` to `MODEL` through `client`. Trim and lowercase the reply. If the result is one of `LABELS`, return it. Otherwise throw an `Error`.

The check labels five sample messages through the local model, reads the system message you send, and feeds `labelMessage` a fake reply that is a full sentence (it must throw) and one with stray spaces and a capital letter (it must return the label).
nextSteps: Send the request with LABEL_PROMPT as the system message and print the raw reply.
Run `node src/demo.ts` while the prompt is still empty and read what the model says.
Write LABEL_PROMPT so the model knows the labels and the reply format, then clean up the reply.
Throw when the cleaned reply is not one of LABELS.
hints: Without instructions the local model answers like a chatty colleague. Your prompt is what changes that.
The local model only switches to bare labels when the system message lists every label and uses the word "only".
`LABELS.includes(...)` needs a small cast in TypeScript, because LABELS is a readonly tuple of exact strings.

tasks.title: Show the format with worked examples
tasks.description:
A label is not enough for the inbox view: Ravi also wants the plant and how urgent the message is. The reply must be one line in exactly this format:

```
label: pests | plant: orchid | urgency: normal
```

Keys are lowercase, separated by ` | `. `label` is one of the five labels, `plant` is the plant in lowercase (or `unknown`), `urgency` is `high` or `normal`.

Write `TRIAGE_PROMPT` and implement `buildTriageMessages(text: string): Message[]`:

- first, a system message with `TRIAGE_PROMPT`
- then at least two worked examples, each a `user` message followed by an `assistant` reply in the exact format above
- last, a `user` message with `text`, unchanged

The check inspects the array and sends it to the local model with five sample messages to see that every reply comes back as a triage line.
nextSteps: Write two short customer messages of your own.
Write the triage line you would want back for each one.
Build the array: system, your examples as user and assistant pairs, then the text.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and compare the replies with your examples.
hints: Describing a format in words is a start. Showing it is what makes a model copy it exactly.
Examples go in the conversation as if the model had already answered them: user, then assistant.
Keep the examples in a constant array of pairs and use flatMap to turn each pair into two messages.

tasks.title: Parse the triage line
tasks.description:
Implement `triage(text: string, client?: OpenAI): Promise<Triage>`.

- Send `buildTriageMessages(text)` to `MODEL` through `client`.
- Trim the reply and parse it as a triage line. Return `{ label, plant, urgency }` and nothing else.
- If the reply is not exactly a triage line (wrong case, commas, a sentence, an unknown label or urgency), throw an `Error`.

The check triages five sample messages through the local model, and feeds `triage` fake replies: a valid line with a two-word plant, a sentence and a near miss with capital letters.
nextSteps: Write a regular expression for the whole line, anchored at both ends.
Capture the label, the plant and the urgency.
Throw when it does not match, then build the result object.
hints: Your code is the one that relies on the format, so it should be strict about it rather than forgiving.
Anchor the pattern with `^` and `$`, and remember that `|` must be escaped to match a literal bar.
The plant capture needs to allow letters and spaces, while label and urgency can list their allowed words.
